bug_description.original: Detailed report: https://oss-fuzz.com/testcase?key=5649010138284032 Project: gnutls Fuzzer: libFuzzer_gnutls_pkcs12_key_parser_fuzzer Fuzz target binary: gnutls_pkcs12_key_parser_fuzzer Job Type: libfuzzer_asan_gnutls Platform Id: linux Crash Type: Heap-use-after-free READ 8 Crash Address: 0x60c000000080 Crash State: gnutls_x509_crl_deinit gnutls_pkcs12_simple_parse _start Sanitizer: address (ASAN) Recommended Security Severity: High
bug_description.normalized: OSS-Fuzz issue 1304: In gnutls_pkcs12_simple_parse, when gnutls_x509_crl_import fails, the code calls gnutls_x509_crl_deinit(*crl) to free the CRL object but does not set *crl to NULL. The subsequent error cleanup at the done: label sees the stale non-NULL pointer, calls gnutls_x509_crl_deinit(*crl) a second time, and reads 8 bytes from the freed heap object at crl.c:98. ASan reports heap-use-after-free READ 8.

source.description: Allocates a CRL object via gnutls_x509_crl_init(crl), storing the heap pointer in *crl. This allocation is triggered when a GNUTLS_BAG_CRL element is found in the PKCS12 bag parsed from the attacker-controlled input.
source.value_from: The PKCS12 DER blob from the fuzzer input triggers the GNUTLS_BAG_CRL case; gnutls_x509_crl_init calloc's a gnutls_x509_crl_int struct into *crl; value `*crl`; from `gnutls_x509_crl_init(crl)`

sink.description: Reads crl->crl (8 bytes) from the already-freed CRL object. This is the second invocation of gnutls_x509_crl_deinit on the same pointer, triggered by the cleanup code at pkcs12.c:1791 which passes the stale *crl value.

root_cause.description: After gnutls_x509_crl_import fails, gnutls_x509_crl_deinit(*crl) frees the CRL object but *crl is not set to NULL. The stale pointer remains in *crl, causing the done: cleanup to call gnutls_x509_crl_deinit a second time on freed memory. The fix adds `*crl = NULL;` after this deinit call.

tainted_value_origin.description: The malformed CRL data from the PKCS12 bag causes gnutls_x509_crl_import to fail (ret < 0), triggering the error path where *crl is freed but not nulled.

coarse_trace.summary: Parses the PKCS12 input, finds a GNUTLS_BAG_CRL element, and enters the CRL initialization and import path.
Allocates a CRL object and attempts import; import fails due to malformed data, triggering deinit of *crl without nulling the pointer.
The done: cleanup sees stale non-NULL *crl and calls gnutls_x509_crl_deinit a second time, accessing freed memory.
Reads crl->crl from the freed 64-byte heap region; ASan detects heap-use-after-free READ 8.

fine_trace.note: The PKCS12 bag element parsed from the attacker-controlled DER input is of type GNUTLS_BAG_CRL. This dispatches into the CRL handling branch, reaching the allocation.

Allocates a 64-byte gnutls_x509_crl_int structure via calloc (crl.c:73) and stores the pointer in *crl. This is the allocation that will be freed twice. ASan confirms: 64-byte region [0x606000000020,0x606000000060) allocated here via calloc in gnutls_x509_crl_init.
Attempts to import the CRL from the bag's DER data. The malformed input causes the import to fail (ret < 0), triggering the error handling path that frees *crl.

depends_on.via: *crl is the heap pointer to free

fine_trace.note: Frees the CRL object. After this call, *crl is a dangling pointer — gnutls_free(crl) inside gnutls_x509_crl_deinit releases the 64-byte heap region. The pointer in *crl is NOT set to NULL. This is the root cause: the missing `*crl = NULL;` statement that the fix adds.
Jumps to the done: cleanup label at line 1781. Since ret < 0, the cleanup block's error-handling path is entered.
The guard checks whether *crl is non-NULL to decide whether to deinitialize it. Because step 4 did not null out *crl, the stale pointer passes this check and the body executes.

depends_on.via: crl argument is the freed pointer from step 4

fine_trace.note: Reads 8 bytes at offset 0 of the freed 64-byte CRL struct to check the crl->crl field. ASan detects: heap-use-after-free READ of size 8 at 0x606000000020, which is 0 bytes inside the freed region. The memory was freed by gnutls_x509_crl_deinit called at pkcs12.c:1745 (step 4).

format.name: libFuzzer binary blob for gnutls_pkcs12_key_parser_fuzzer
format.contract: A malformed PKCS12 DER blob that contains a private key (passes the first-loop key extraction) and a GNUTLS_BAG_CRL element whose CRL data fails gnutls_x509_crl_import. The import failure triggers the double-free path unconditionally once *crl is allocated and the import returns a negative error code.

parser_admitted.description: The PKCS12 DER import must succeed (ret >= 0) so execution reaches gnutls_pkcs12_simple_parse.

private_key_found.description: A private key must be found in the PKCS12 bags (privkey_ok == 1) so the function proceeds to the certificate/CRL iteration loop rather than returning early.

crl_bag_reached.description: A GNUTLS_BAG_CRL element must be present and *crl must be NULL (first CRL encountered) to enter the CRL initialization branch.
